facts.text: Stoneville hosts the Delta Research and Extension Center, a major Mississippi State University facility that began in 1904 as an agricultural experiment station.
In Stoneville, the Delta Research and Extension Center grew from a 200‑acre plot to nearly 5,000 acres, now housing labs, greenhouses, and experimental fields.
In Stoneville, the center pioneered calcium arsenate dusting to fight the boll weevil in the 1930s, moving from mule‑drawn to tractor‑ and aerial‑applied methods.
Stoneville’s early economy relied on cotton, with steamboats on Deer Creek transporting bales before railroads took over.
The town was incorporated in 1882 but later lost its incorporated status, yet it still maintains a post office opened in 1876.
Johnny “Big Moose” Walker, a blues musician, hails from Stoneville, adding a musical legacy to the town’s history.
